scope: Definitions and research leads only. No existing detector implementation or real-song tag assignment is claimed.

entries.definition: Community-named slide/tap coordination family. Exact event grammar, admissible variants and boundaries require review; this is not a synonym for every tap occurring during a slide.
entries.detector_proposal: Review the two named tutorials or accessible equivalent primary explanations; identify exact chart variants and sections; record event-role, phase and spatial constraints plus hard negatives. Only then implement a versioned motif recognizer.
counterexamples_and_limits: Any generic slide/tap overlap is insufficient.
Song-title matching must never assign this tag.
Name attestation is not detector validation.

entries.definition: A monophonic sequence alternating between two distinct positions with a locally regular onset spacing. Trill is a descriptive label here; this seed does not assert a universal maimai definition.
entries.detector_proposal: Start with at least six onsets alternating A/B; match spacing in beat units with explicit tolerance and permit documented break/EX flags without changing the motif.
counterexamples_and_limits: Two notes alone are not a trill.
Simultaneous A+B chords are not an alternating stream.
Do not infer actual left/right hand assignment.

entries.definition: Three or more separate onsets repeatedly directed to the same button or explicitly supported touch location.
entries.detector_proposal: Find same-position runs, storing spacing and run length; split across a configurable long gap and preserve event type.
counterexamples_and_limits: One hold is not repeated tapping.
Duplicate parser events must be removed before detection.

entries.definition: Repeated two-onset groups with a short within-pair interval followed by a longer inter-pair interval. This operational label follows the user suggestion rather than claiming a maimai-standard taxonomy.
entries.detector_proposal: Proposed seed: at least three pairs, with a consistent long/short spacing ratio near 2 or 3 under a versioned tolerance. Store ratio and orientation; do not require particular hand use.
counterexamples_and_limits: A uniform trill is not a gallop.
Three notes are not automatically musical triplets.
Do not equate every swung rhythm with this motif.

entries.definition: A locally grouped burst of three onsets separated from neighboring activity by longer gaps.
entries.detector_proposal: Compare within-group and outside gaps using explicit beat-relative thresholds; store all three event roles and positions.
counterexamples_and_limits: A group of three is not necessarily triplet subdivision.
Chord cardinality is not sequential burst length.

entries.definition: A run aligned to a three-part subdivision of a validated local beat grid.
entries.detector_proposal: Match event phases to rational thirds (or documented finer triplet subdivisions), requiring several successive intervals and a valid beat anchor.
counterexamples_and_limits: Unknown beat anchor yields unknown.
Three arbitrary notes do not establish triplet rhythm.

entries.definition: A repeated run on an explicitly defined non-downbeat phase of a validated beat grid.
entries.detector_proposal: Record phase distribution and require repeated nonzero phase; split at tempo/grid changes when continuity is not known.
counterexamples_and_limits: BPM alone does not establish the musical downbeat.
Do not call a chart syncopated solely from a shifted global offset.

entries.definition: Two or more distinct input onsets authored at the same time, with event type and positions retained.
entries.detector_proposal: Use authored simultaneous groups or exact normalized timing; count unique physical onset events and preserve source pseudo-simultaneous distinctions.
counterexamples_and_limits: Near-simultaneous decorative notes are not necessarily a chord.
A shared slide head is not several taps.

entries.definition: Several simultaneous-note groups occurring in sequence.
entries.detector_proposal: Group at least three repeated simultaneous events and store changes in cardinality, positions and spacing.
counterexamples_and_limits: Do not claim a fixed two-hand solution.
Different group shapes are retained, not flattened.

entries.definition: A sequence stepping through neighboring perimeter buttons in a consistent direction over a bounded arc.
entries.detector_proposal: Match at least four distinct neighbor steps on circular button coordinates, preserving direction and modulo wrap.
counterexamples_and_limits: One long slide is not a tap staircase.
Do not prescribe a hand crossover.

entries.definition: A tap sequence progressing around a substantial part of the outer button ring.
entries.detector_proposal: Extend adjacent-step analysis with cumulative angular travel and run length; distinguish full circuits from partial arcs.
counterexamples_and_limits: Visual rotation alone is insufficient.
A fan slide is not a perimeter tap run.

entries.definition: A perimeter tap run that changes its traversal direction within the local phrase.
entries.detector_proposal: Find adjacent-step runs with a sustained sign change in angular increments; preserve both phrase lengths.
counterexamples_and_limits: One repeated button is not a direction change.
The shortest geometric path need not be the player hand path.

entries.definition: Two or more slide branches attached to the same authored head event.
entries.detector_proposal: Use shared-head IDs and separate path IDs; store branch count, waiting and movement overlaps without duplicating the head tap.
counterexamples_and_limits: Different heads at the same timestamp are not a shared head.
Multiple branches do not prove more hands are required.

entries.definition: Slide movement intervals with unequal start times that overlap in time.
entries.detector_proposal: Sweep movement interval endpoints; require positive interval overlap and distinct movement starts, then store phase separation.
counterexamples_and_limits: Simultaneous visual appearance is not movement overlap.
A slide waiting to move must not be counted as already moving.

entries.definition: At least two slide paths moving concurrently for a nonzero interval.
entries.detector_proposal: Use half-open movement intervals; store duration, maximum concurrency, shared-head relationship and any separately supported geometry overlap.
counterexamples_and_limits: Waiting intervals are separate.
Concurrency does not prove crossing hands or occlusion.

entries.definition: Distinct tap onsets occurring during another slide movement interval.
entries.detector_proposal: Join taps to active slide intervals, exclude the slide own head and documented co-trigger equivalences; retain spatial relations where supported.
counterexamples_and_limits: This is not sufficient for the Umiyuri tag.
Temporal overlap alone does not establish two independent hand actions.

entries.definition: Other tap onsets between a slide head and that slide movement start.
entries.detector_proposal: Join independent onsets into the open waiting interval and preserve waiting length and spatial roles.
counterexamples_and_limits: Taps during movement belong to a different detector.
Default delay alone is not automatically unusual timing.

entries.definition: A local series switching between distinct head-to-movement waiting intervals in beat units or explicitly authored seconds.
entries.detector_proposal: Cluster successive waiting values using explicit tolerances and retain tempo context; distinguish absolute-time and beat-based declarations.
counterexamples_and_limits: Tempo change can alter seconds without changing beat-relative structure.
Unsupported waiting syntax produces unknown.

entries.definition: An authored connected slide with multiple sequential path segments.
entries.detector_proposal: Use explicit chain and segment IDs; preserve segment timings, connectivity and any missing local geometry.
counterexamples_and_limits: Adjacent unrelated slides are not automatically one connected chain.
Segment count is not note count.

entries.definition: Independent tap onsets occurring while a hold or supported touch hold is active.
entries.detector_proposal: Join unique taps to hold intervals, keeping location and input type; do not count a hold as repeated taps.
counterexamples_and_limits: Do not assign a holding hand from aggregate geometry alone.

entries.definition: A hold interval and a slide movement interval overlap.
entries.detector_proposal: Calculate overlap intervals, spatial context when supported, and duration; distinguish wait from movement.
counterexamples_and_limits: Overlap is a structural observation, not proof of an impossible input combination.

entries.definition: A locally interleaved sequence of inner touch and perimeter-button onsets.
entries.detector_proposal: Match alternating or mixed runs with documented locality/gap limits and retain touch-zone identity.
counterexamples_and_limits: Touch/button switching is not measured hand travel.
Missing touch-zone geometry limits movement interpretations.

entries.definition: A large rate of distinct authored input onsets under a stated absolute scale or named reference cohort.
entries.detector_proposal: Measure unweighted unique onset count per effective second over fixed windows; attach scale/reference ID and threshold.
counterexamples_and_limits: Break score value is not extra physical note count.
This does not measure total difficulty.

entries.definition: Short high-density passages contrasted with lower-density sections.
entries.detector_proposal: Use short-window peak-to-background ratio plus absolute floor and minimum separation, storing affected intervals.
counterexamples_and_limits: Very low baseline alone must not produce a dramatic burst label.
A density burst is not a diagnosis of stamina demand.

entries.definition: A long contiguous period above an explicitly documented density threshold.
entries.detector_proposal: Measure longest and total qualifying duration with a small, versioned gap-merging rule.
counterexamples_and_limits: Unknown chart span must be reported.
Long holds alone do not establish high onset density.

entries.definition: The latter part of the analyzed span contains substantially more measured onset activity than the beginning.
entries.detector_proposal: Compare duration-weighted early/late density and center of mass, with absolute contrast requirements and explicit span basis.
counterexamples_and_limits: Call this backloaded density, not guaranteed ending difficulty.
An uncertain audio tail must not shift classification silently.

entries.definition: The earlier part of the analyzed span contains substantially more measured onset activity than the ending.
entries.detector_proposal: Mirror the documented backloaded-density decision rule and store early/late values.
counterexamples_and_limits: Song audio duration and note span are not interchangeable.

entries.definition: One separated peak dominates the density profile under a stated peak detector.
entries.detector_proposal: Require prominence, minimum duration, neighboring lower activity and a single dominant qualifying peak.
counterexamples_and_limits: Do not smooth away a short spike.
This tag says nothing about pattern teachability without separate evidence.

entries.definition: Two or more separated prominent density peaks.
entries.detector_proposal: Store peak intervals and prominence rather than only a binary tag; use a versioned separation criterion.
counterexamples_and_limits: Tiny numerical ripples are not separate meaningful peaks.

entries.definition: Density varies relatively little through the analyzed span, with a nontrivial activity floor.
entries.detector_proposal: Use robust relative variation and coverage thresholds; report absolute density separately.
counterexamples_and_limits: An empty chart is not a steady practice chart.
Steady density does not imply easy execution.

entries.definition: Intervals with few new onsets, with any active holds/slides reported separately.
entries.detector_proposal: Locate low-onset windows and annotate residual active movement/hold occupancy.
counterexamples_and_limits: Low onset count during ongoing slides is not necessarily a rest.

entries.definition: Concentration of source-flagged break events within sections of the chart.
entries.detector_proposal: Measure event counts, fraction and temporal concentration by supported event type; no rating-rule weighting in the player-independent analyzer.
counterexamples_and_limits: Break value must not inflate physical density.
Scoring risk requires a separate version-aware rating/scoring interpretation.

entries.definition: Substantial changes among beat-relative inter-onset intervals in local phrases.
entries.detector_proposal: Measure interval distributions and transition frequency with motif/tempo context; preserve observable values.
counterexamples_and_limits: Entropy alone is not musical complexity.
Tempo changes are not automatically harder rhythm.

entries.definition: A large fraction of the analyzed span has at least one slide path moving.
entries.detector_proposal: Integrate the union of slide movement intervals, report concurrency separately, and attach the threshold and span basis.
counterexamples_and_limits: Many visible waiting slides are not moving occupancy.
High occupancy does not imply a named motif.

entries.definition: A structural phrase appears repeatedly under a documented exact or normalized matching policy.
entries.detector_proposal: Compare event-role/phase signatures with explicit rotation, reflection and tempo-normalization settings; retain all matching sections.
counterexamples_and_limits: Rotation and reflection are not always equally playable.
Shared broad tags are not sufficient to assert repetition.

entries.definition: Occurrences of a target motif have relatively few competing event roles or demands around them.
entries.detector_proposal: Calculate a target-specific surrounding-activity vector; require supported motif identification and explicit temporal neighborhood.
counterexamples_and_limits: This is target-specific, not a universal chart property.
Isolation supports a practice hypothesis; it does not prove learning effectiveness.
